tier_reason: py-pdf/benchmarks is an independent third-party suite (py-pdf organisation, BSD-3-Clause) whose public harness (benchmark.py, pdf_benchmark/library_code.py) times PyMuPDF, the poppler pdftotext tool and pypdfium2 on the same 14 PDFs on a stated CPU (Intel Core i7-6700HQ); compiler and flags are not stated (prebuilt PyPI wheels and a distro poppler-utils binary), so it falls short of A.

corrections.baseline: poppler (the pdftotext command-line tool from poppler-utils, run as a subprocess) and PDFium (via pypdfium2)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: not stated: PyMuPDF 1.28.2 and pypdfium2 5.13.0 are prebuilt PyPI wheels; pdftotext is the system /usr/bin/pdftotext binary, which HISTORY.md records as Poppler 24.02.0 (the README's '0.86.1' is a hard-coded label in benchmark.py)
corrections.claimed_speedup: Text extraction average 0.1 s for PyMuPDF against 0.3 s for pdftotext (poppler); per document 0.3 s against 1.0 s (GeoTopo-book) and 0.2 s against 0.8 s (1707.09725); from the suite's cache.json the 14-document totals are 1.604 s for PyMuPDF against 4.008 s for pdftotext (about 2.5x, derived from page data). pypdfium2 (PDFium) ties PyMuPDF at 0.1 s average and is ranked first (1.591 s total, marginally faster). Image extraction average 0.5 s for PyMuPDF against 1.0 s for pypdfium2 (7.333 s against 14.523 s total in cache.json, about 2x, derived from page data); poppler is not in the image row.
corrections.caveats: Independent suite (py-pdf organisation, BSD-3-Clause, runs the same script for every library; code public) but compiler and flags are not stated, so it is B not A. Harness: one run per document timed with time.time(), no warm-up or repetition, results rounded to 0.1 s in the README (raw seconds are in cache.json); the poppler row is not libpoppler-cpp but the /usr/bin/pdftotext binary launched with subprocess after writing the PDF to a temp file, so it pays process start-up and temp-file I/O that the in-process PyMuPDF and pypdfium2 calls do not (too small to explain the 2.5x total gap, since small documents show pdftotext at 0.0-0.1 s); pypdfium2 text timings include Python post-processing that PyMuPDF's do not. The README's Libraries table labels pdftotext '0.86.1' (hard-coded in benchmark.py) while HISTORY.md says Poppler 24.02.0. PDFium ties MuPDF on text extraction and is ranked first, so the text-extraction win is over poppler only; the image-extraction win is over PDFium only (poppler not measured there), and the two image paths (PyMuPDF extract_image versus pypdfium2 PdfImage.extract) are not checked for equivalent output. The measured jobs are text and image extraction through Python bindings, not page rasterisation, so category rasterizers-2d is a best fit and neither baseline is in that category's list (Skia, Cairo, Blend2D); the orchestrator may prefer a document-parsing category. First-party rendering evidence also exists: PyMuPDF docs Appendix 4 (https://github.com/pymupdf/PyMuPDF/blob/main/docs/app4.rst) report 150 DPI page rendering totals of 367.04 s for PyMuPDF against 646 s for XPDF pdftopng.exe (rate 1.76) and 851.52 s for pdf2jpg across eight sample PDFs, and plain text extraction 8.01 s against 27.42 s for XPDF (3.42x); that page states no CPU, compiler or date, includes file-writing time, and XPDF is poppler's ancestor rather than poppler, so it is tier C and was not used as the headline. The PDF Association survey (pdfa.org, 2021) and an Alfresco blog compare MuPDF, poppler and PDFium rendering but both hosts are blocked here, so their figures were not read. The GitHub repository is a mirror of Artifex's own git server; AGPL-3.0 with commercial licensing from Artifex.

notes: All claimed numbers match the py-pdf/benchmarks README and its cache.json; MuPDF beats poppler's pdftotext about 2.5x on total text-extraction time and pypdfium2 about 2x on image extraction, but ties PDFium on text extraction (PDFium ranked first). Shortcomings to record: poppler timed as a subprocess CLI with temp-file I/O, single unrepeated runs rounded to 0.1 s, stale '0.86.1' pdftotext label, extraction rather than rasterisation, baselines outside the rasterizers-2d list.
